the initial outgrowth of chick sympathetic neurites on polyornithincoated substrates requires contact of the neurite tips with a three-dimensional object, and that the cytoplasm invades the tips of filopodia on polyornithinedcoated substrates when the filopodia are closely apposed to the substrate only at their tips.

neurite formation by sympathetic neurons grown on laminin is initiated by cytoplasm invasion of filopodia, whereas neurite formation on polyornithines is initiated by cytoskeletal rearrangements in filopodia.
neurite initiation requires adhesion of the cytoplasm to a substrate, and that the adhesion must occur only at the tip of the filopodium.

the mechanisms by which neuronal cytoplasm is organized into processes, the neurites.
understanding the mechanisms by which the cytoskeleton is organized and regulated during neuronal development.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the initial events in neurite formation are: (a) filopodia are formed and (b) filopodia contact the substrate and then cytoplasm is pushed into the filopodia.
neurite formation is initiated by the interaction of filopodial cytoskeleton and substratum.
the initial formation of neurites by chick sympathetic neurons in culture requires the interaction of cytoplasmic components, including actin filaments and neurofilaments, with the substrate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the initiation of neurite growth is a two-step process.

neurite outgrowth begins with the invasion of the actomyosin cores of filipodia by cytoplams containing microtubles and neurofilaments, and that this cytoplasmic invasion is triggered by the adhesion of the filopodia tip to the substrate.
neurite outgrowth is initiated when the filopodial tip is attached to the substrate and the cytoskeletal core is pushed into the filopodial shaft by the force of actin polymerization.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cytoplasm invasion of filopodia is a key step in neurite initiation, and this invasion is initiated when filopodia make close contact with substrates.
neurite formation does not require specific cell adhesion molecule mediated interactions between the neuron and the growth substrate.

the initiation of neurite formation is a process that is initiated by the interaction between the actin cytoskeleton of filopodia and the growth substrate, and that the interaction between the cytoskeletal elements of filopodia is not sufficient to initiate the process of neurite out growth.
